stemMd: Fungi were once classified as plants. Which statement correctly describes a difference between the two kingdoms?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Fungi are prokaryotes, whereas plants are eukaryotes

options.label: B
options.textMd: Fungi carry out photosynthesis using a pigment other than chlorophyll

options.label: C
options.textMd: Fungi are heterotrophs with cell walls made of chitin, not cellulose

options.label: D
options.textMd: Fungal cells have no cell wall, whereas plant cells have one

options.label: E
options.textMd: Fungi store carbohydrate mainly as starch, whereas plants store it as glycogen

explanationMd:
Compare the two kingdoms feature by feature.

| Feature | Plants | Fungi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cell type | eukaryotic | eukaryotic |
| Nutrition | autotrophic (photosynthesis) | heterotrophic, by absorption |
| Cell wall | cellulose | chitin |
| Carbohydrate store | starch | glycogen |

Fungi secrete enzymes into their surroundings and absorb the products, as moulds do on bread; they cannot photosynthesise. Their walls are made of **chitin**, the same polysaccharide found in insect exoskeletons.

**Check:** only one statement matches the table; each of the others gets a row wrong, or swaps the two kingdoms.

distractorRationale.a: Both fungi and plants are eukaryotes, with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Prokaryotes are bacteria and archaea.
distractorRationale.b: Fungi have no photosynthetic pigment at all; they are heterotrophs that feed on organic matter made by other organisms.
distractorRationale.d: Fungal cells do have a cell wall; it is made of chitin instead of the cellulose found in plants.
distractorRationale.e: This swaps the two storage molecules: plants store starch, while fungi, like animals, store glycogen.

accessibilityText: A short text question with no figure. Fungi were once classified as plants, and the question asks which statement correctly describes a difference between the two kingdoms. The choices are: fungi are prokaryotes whereas plants are eukaryotes; fungi photosynthesise using a pigment other than chlorophyll; fungi are heterotrophs with cell walls made of chitin, not cellulose; fungal cells have no cell wall whereas plant cells have one; fungi store carbohydrate mainly as starch whereas plants store glycogen. The explanation contains a table comparing plants and fungi by cell type, nutrition, cell wall and carbohydrate store.

provenance.notes: Original item. Tests the defining features of the kingdom Fungi against plants.
